item.title: Leaner, steadier PHPUnit runs for upcoming releases
item.description:
WordPress core has optimized its GitHub Actions PHPUnit CI pipeline to reduce job volume and improve reliability ahead of the 7.1 release. The changes trim the test matrix to boundary PHP versions, drop redundant database combinations, and cache the Gutenberg build across jobs instead of rebuilding it per job. This cuts per-run job counts by roughly half and slashes rerun rates from ~68% to ~36%, freeing CI capacity for release windows and daily development.
Digest entry: issues/dev-notes/make-core-125103.md · Source: Make WordPress Core

item.title: jQuery UI updated to 1.14.2 in WordPress 7.1
item.description:
WordPress 7.1 upgrades the bundled jQuery UI library from version 1.13.3 to 1.14.2. This update aligns with WordPress’s browser support policy by dropping legacy Internet Explorer and Edge support. To maintain backward compatibility with older jQuery UI patterns, the library now initializes with `jQuery.uiBackCompat` set to `true`.
Digest entry: issues/dev-notes/make-core-124739.md · Source: Make WordPress Core

item.title: New execution lifecycle filters for the Abilities API in WordPress 7.1
item.description:
WordPress 7.1 adds four new filters to the Abilities API that let plugins intercept and modify the execution lifecycle of registered abilities. The hooks—`wp_pre_execute_ability`, `wp_ability_normalize_input`, `wp_ability_permission_result`, and `wp_ability_execute_result`—enable short-circuiting execution, transforming input, overriding permission checks, and recovering or sanitizing results before schema validation. This makes the API significantly more extensible for caching, rate limiting, additional authorization layers, and AI/automation integrations without requiring custom ability implementations.
Digest entry: issues/dev-notes/make-core-125000.md · Source: Make WordPress Core

item.title: Dev Chat Agenda – July 28, 2026
item.description:
The WordPress 7.1 release cycle is advancing toward Beta 4, with the developers chat agenda highlighting several upcoming core capabilities. Key additions include client-side media processing, text shadow support in global styles, default infinite scroll for the media library, editable blocks inside the Custom HTML block, and new block supports for minimum width and background gradients. These changes will be documented in individual dev notes as they merge.
Digest entry: issues/dev-notes/make-core-124970.md · Source: Make WordPress Core

item.title: New Block Support in WordPress 7.1: Background Gradient (background.gradient)
item.description:
WordPress 7.1 introduces a new `background.gradient` block support that allows gradients to render alongside background images on the same block. Previously, gradients applied via `color.gradient` used the `background` shorthand, which reset and overrode any `background-image`. The new support stores values at `style.background.gradient` and renders via the `background-image` longhand property, enabling comma-separated gradient and image declarations without conflict.
Digest entry: issues/dev-notes/make-core-124676.md · Source: Make WordPress Core

item.title: New Block Support in WordPress 7.1: Minimum Width
item.description:
WordPress 7.1 adds a `minWidth` dimension block support, allowing blocks to enforce a minimum width constraint natively. This fills a gap in the existing dimension controls by mirroring the `minHeight` support, applying the `min-width` CSS property to the block wrapper. Theme authors and block developers can now expose this constraint through the Dimensions panel without relying on custom CSS or block styles.
Digest entry: issues/dev-notes/make-core-124685.md · Source: Make WordPress Core

item.title: Registering and rendering SVG icons in WordPress 7.1
item.description:
WordPress 7.1 introduces a formal public API for managing and rendering SVG icons, moving beyond the 7.0 built-in set. Developers can now register custom icon collections, add individual icons via inline markup or file paths, render them server-side, and expose them to the editor and REST API. This standardizes icon handling across plugins, themes, and core blocks.
Digest entry: issues/dev-notes/make-core-124593.md · Source: Make WordPress Core

item.title: React 19: punted beyond WordPress 7.1, experiment in Gutenberg
item.description:
WordPress 7.1 will ship with React 18.3, deferring the React 19 upgrade to a future release. An initial attempt to upgrade was reverted after testing revealed incompatibilities when React 18 and 19 coexist in the same environment, particularly with how plugins bundle and consume React. Gutenberg 23.4+ now includes an experimental flag to enable React 19 for plugin compatibility testing.
Digest entry: issues/dev-notes/make-core-124768.md · Source: Make WordPress Core

item.title: WP2Shell WordPress Exploit Technical Analysis and Real Attack Data
item.description:
WordPress core patched a critical vulnerability chain that allowed unauthenticated attackers to create an administrator account and subsequently execute arbitrary code. The chain combined an SQL injection in the `author__not_in` parameter (CVE-2026-60137) with a REST API batch request route confusion flaw (CVE-2026-63030). The Security Team issued forced automatic updates to close the gap across affected 6.8, 6.9, and 7.0 releases.
Digest entry: issues/security/wordfence-blog-42579.md · Source: Wordfence Blog

item.title: Demi <= 0.0.6 - Unauthenticated Arbitrary Directory Deletion via demi_restore_step AJAX action
item.description:
The Demi – One Click Demo Import, Backup & Site Migration plugin contained a critical unauthenticated arbitrary directory deletion vulnerability (CVE-2026-14490) in versions up to 0.0.7. The flaw allowed attackers to recursively delete arbitrary server directories by exploiting the `demi_restore_step` AJAX endpoint, which bypassed standard WordPress capability and nonce checks when an attacker possessed an exposed HMAC signing key. The vulnerability has been patched in version 0.0.9 by restricting the AJAX handler to authenticated requests, enforcing strict path canonicalization and allow-listing, and securing the storage of signing keys and restore tokens.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-63922c28-0cb5-4abe-85ee-20b2cc6f015d.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: SMS Alert <= 3.9.7 - Unauthenticated Authentication Bypass to Account Takeover via 'billing_phone' Parameter
item.description:
The SMS Alert plugin (≤ 3.9.7) contained a critical authentication bypass that allowed unauthenticated attackers to take over any existing WordPress account by exploiting the `billing_phone` parameter during registration. The vulnerability stemmed from `processRegistration()` setting a session flag (`$_SESSION['sa_mobile_verified']`) upon OTP validation without binding it to the verified phone number, allowing an attacker to verify their own number and then swap in a victim's phone to trigger `wp_set_auth_cookie()` for the victim's account. This issue has been resolved in version 3.9.8 by properly binding the verification state to the specific phone number and validating it before issuing authentication cookies.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-661d4ea9-572d-4544-b5cf-39fd69c104a6.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: Advanced Responsive Video Embedder for Rumble, Odysee, YouTube, Vimeo, Kick … 10.8.7 - Unauthenticated Authentication Bypass via Hardcoded Backdoor in '_wplogin' Parameter
item.description:
The Advanced Responsive Video Embedder plugin (v10.8.7) contains a hardcoded backdoor that allows unauthenticated users to bypass WordPress authentication and assume any existing administrator role. The vulnerability stems from the `_arve_uc_init()` function, which runs on the `init` hook at priority 1 and validates a static SHA-256 hash against the `_wplogin` (or `_wpm`) request parameter. Because the hash is embedded directly in the plugin source, attackers can supply the known token to gain full administrative control without credentials.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-70f64ea0-5375-479f-90ac-29bcdf817cef.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: Spreadsheet Price Changer for WooCommerce and WP E-commerce – Light <= 2.4.37 - Missing Authorization to Unauthenticated Privilege Escalation via Admin Account Creation
item.description:
The `user_filter` function in Spreadsheet Price Changer for WooCommerce and WP E-commerce – Light (≤ 2.4.37) lacks authorization checks, allowing unauthenticated users to create new administrator accounts. This missing authorization enables immediate privilege escalation without requiring any credentials. The plugin author has not released a patch, so the only mitigation is to remove the plugin or switch to an alternative.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-1f891b68-72c4-4f94-bd49-52576ad710f9.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: Cost Calculator Builder PRO <= 4.0.3 - Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution via 'orderDetails' Parameter
item.description:
The Cost Calculator Builder PRO plugin contained a critical unauthenticated remote code execution vulnerability in versions up to 4.0.3. Attackers could exploit the `js_to_php` function by injecting malicious payloads into the `orderDetails[*].originalValue` field, which was passed directly to `PHP eval()` without proper sanitization. The vulnerability was patched in version 4.0.4, and all affected sites must update immediately to prevent server compromise.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-4c8f2872-06ff-41a2-b601-77a47470de0c.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: Meta Box AIO <= 3.8.0 - Missing Authorization to Unauthenticated Arbitrary Post Deletion via 'rwmb_frontend_field_object_id' Parameter
item.description:
Meta Box AIO versions up to 3.8.0 contain a critical missing-authorization vulnerability in the MB Frontend Submission extension that allows unauthenticated attackers to delete arbitrary posts and pages. The flaw occurs because the `handle_request()` function processes the `mbfs_delete` action without verifying user capabilities or post ownership, and the nonce check is bypassed when requests arrive via `template_redirect` instead of AJAX. Site owners must update to version 3.9.0 or later to prevent unauthorized content deletion.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-e9506f84-3d33-48e0-8dce-d517e1a923e4.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: Admin and Site Enhancements (ASE) Pro <= 8.9.0 - Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution via PHP Code Injection via cfgroup[input] Repeater Row Key
item.description:
The Admin and Site Enhancements (ASE) Pro plugin contained an unauthenticated remote code execution vulnerability in versions up to 8.9.0. The flaw allowed attackers to inject arbitrary PHP code via the `cfgroup[input]` repeater row key, which was passed unsanitized into an `eval()` call inside the `recursive_html` function. The vulnerability required the `[post_cf_form]` shortcode to be present on a public page to emit the necessary nonce and session ID. Patched in version 8.9.1, this fix eliminates a critical server-side execution risk for sites using the plugin's form builder.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-2ef21a44-6d03-4197-b49c-d881f9831f46.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: Realtyna Organic IDX plugin + WPL Real Estate <= 5.2.0 - Unauthenticated Arbitrary File Upload via 'files[file]' Parameter via Public I/O 'set_property' Command
item.description:
The Realtyna Organic IDX plugin + WPL Real Estate (≤ 5.2.0) contains an unauthenticated arbitrary file upload vulnerability that enables remote code execution. The flaw stems from a publicly registered I/O endpoint that lacks WordPress capability checks and accepts uploads via the `files[file]` parameter without validating file types. Attackers can exploit static, globally shared API credentials to bypass authentication entirely, making immediate mitigation or removal critical for affected installations.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-23068a98-623d-4eb3-a7c5-6af410de4320.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: FormGent <= 1.9.2- Missing Authorization to Unauthenticated Arbitrary File Deletion via 'file_token' Parameter
item.description:
The FormGent plugin contained a critical missing authorization vulnerability that allowed unauthenticated attackers to delete arbitrary files via the `file_token` parameter on the `/wp-json/formgent/responses/attachments` REST endpoint. The issue stemmed from the route being registered without authentication middleware, which also permitted path traversal bypasses on systems where the plugin’s upload directory had not yet been created. This has been resolved in version 1.10.0 by enforcing proper capability checks and validating file paths before deletion.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-097a9d0f-fa38-4fdc-9048-43dd65e7652c.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: Single Sign On For TNG <= 2.0.0 - Unauthenticated Privilege Escalation via Unverified Password Change
item.description:
The Single Sign On For TNG plugin (≤ 2.0.0) contained a critical unauthenticated privilege escalation vulnerability that allowed attackers to reset any user’s password, including administrators, without verification. The flaw stemmed from the `ssoprocess_ajax()` AJAX handler accepting a `setnewpassword` operation and calling WordPress’s `reset_password()` function without validating account ownership or requiring a secure token. Patched in version 2.1.0, this change closes an unverified password reset path that could lead to complete site takeover.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-1d8d393e-764c-491d-8afb-7d4f8d0c387a.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: WooCommerce - Social Login <= 2.8.7 - Unauthenticated Authentication Bypass via Forged Apple 'id_token' JWT
item.description:
The WooCommerce Social Login plugin (≤2.8.7) contained a critical authentication bypass that allowed unauthenticated attackers to log in as any existing WordPress user, including administrators. The vulnerability stemmed from the Apple login handler accepting a forged `id_token` JWT without verifying its cryptographic signature or validating standard claims like issuer, audience, and expiry. Because the handler resolved users solely by the email address in the decoded payload, attackers could craft a token with an admin’s email to hijack sessions. Updating to 2.8.8 is required to restore secure OAuth/JWT validation.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-53e83037-2cc5-4dc9-b55d-03829df12a65.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: Fluent Forms Pro 6.2.7 & Ninja Tables Pro 5.2.13 - Remote Code Execution via Backdoor
item.description:
Versions 6.2.7 of Fluent Forms Pro Add On Pack and 5.2.11 of Ninja Tables Pro shipped with a malicious backdoor embedded by threat actors who compromised the vendor’s build environment. The injected code enabled unauthenticated remote code execution on affected WordPress sites. Patched releases (6.2.8 and 5.2.13) remove the payload and restore secure plugin behavior.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-c6ee9437-a12a-476b-9a4b-8da8d9fbfeb3.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: Membership Plugin – Kadence Memberships <= 4.0.0 - Unauthenticated Password Reset Link Poisoning to Account Takeover
item.description:
The Kadence Memberships plugin (≤4.0.0) contained a critical unauthenticated vulnerability allowing password reset link poisoning, which could lead to full account takeover. The legacy password reset handler accepted an attacker-controlled `rc_redirect` POST parameter and passed it directly to `wp_redirect()` and `add_query_arg()` without validation. When a victim clicked the poisoned reset link, the reset key was exfiltrated to the attacker, who could then replay it to hijack the account. This issue is patched in version 4.0.1.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-ca38c423-2df8-4f20-bd95-2ecd84167a7f.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: Multi Uploader for Gravity Forms <= 1.1.8 - Missing Authorization to Unauthenticated Arbitrary Media Deletion
item.description:
The Multi Uploader for Gravity Forms plugin (≤ 1.1.8) contained a critical authorization flaw allowing unauthenticated attackers to permanently delete any WordPress media attachment. The vulnerability stemmed from a missing capability check in the AJAX handler, combined with a CSRF nonce that was inadvertently exposed to the public via a JavaScript object. The issue was resolved in version 1.1.9 by enforcing proper capability verification and restricting nonce exposure.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-16dca898-1a98-4e0b-8f48-dc01ba2dc4e6.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: Easy Post Submission <= 2.3.0 - Missing Authorization
item.description:
The Easy Post Submission plugin (≤ 2.3.0) contains a critical missing authorization vulnerability that allows unauthenticated users to modify or unpublish arbitrary posts. The `rbsm_submit_post` AJAX endpoint accepts a `postId` parameter and updates post metadata without verifying user capabilities. Patched in 2.4.0, this flaw enables attackers to alter titles, content, excerpts, taxonomies, and force post statuses to draft.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-15494ccf-7c9d-4566-9e80-2da94172a3dd.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: #81618: Admin UI: Fix the primary color of the Fresh admin color scheme
item.description:
The `fresh` entry in `@wordpress/admin-ui`'s admin theme color map was seeded with `#3858e9` — the Modern scheme's primary — so users on the default Fresh admin color scheme saw the Modern accent throughout the block editors instead of the classic WordPress blue. This PR changes that single map entry to `#007cba`, matching what Fresh's stylesheets have always produced. The regression surfaced because Fresh has no `body.admin-color-fresh` rule in the `wordpress-admin-schemes()` Sass mixin, so its accent resolves to the `:root` fallback in `_default-custom-properties.scss` (`#007cba`), while `ThemeProvider` emits `--wp-admin-theme-color` as an inline style that overrode that fallback with the wrong seeded value.
Digest entry: issues/gutenberg/gh-gutenberg-81618.md · Source: WordPress/gutenberg

item.title: #81541: Media editor: keep initial modal focus on the dialog frame
item.description:
The "Edit media" modal was stealing initial focus away from its dialog frame and dropping it onto the crop area once the image finished loading. `MediaEditorCanvas` passed `focusOnMount={ focusOnMount && status === 'loaded' }` down to `Cropper`, and because that gate flips asynchronously — after `Modal` has already focused the dialog frame — focus landed mid-content on the `role="group"` "Crop area", skipping the dialog title and header actions, and could yank focus away from whatever control the user had tabbed to while the image streamed in. The fix removes the `focusOnMount` prop from `MediaEditorCanvas` entirely, so the modal keeps its default `Modal` focus behaviour and the crop area is only reachable by tabbing to it.
Digest entry: issues/gutenberg/gh-gutenberg-81541.md · Source: WordPress/gutenberg

item.title: #81457: Theme: Avoid root-level relational selectors
item.description:
The `@wordpress/theme` package forwarded a root `ThemeProvider`'s `cornerRadius` preset to `<html>` using relational CSS — `:root:has([data-wpds-root-provider="true"][data-wpds-corner-radius="…"])` — which showed up as repeated relational matching in style-recalculation profiles during block selection. This PR removes those `:has()` selectors: `ThemeProvider`'s existing root layout effect now mirrors `data-wpds-root-provider="true"` and `data-wpds-corner-radius="<preset>"` directly onto the owning document's `documentElement`, and the generated token CSS matches with a plain compound selector `:root[data-wpds-root-provider="true"][data-wpds-corner-radius="…"]` at the same specificity. Token resolution for root and nested providers is unchanged; the win is purely in selector-matching cost. Measured at roughly 5% improvement on block-selection style recalculation in the reporter's re-test.
Digest entry: issues/gutenberg/gh-gutenberg-81457.md · Source: WordPress/gutenberg

item.title: #80852: Global Styles: Expose additional elements in Typography and Colors
item.description:
The `cite`, `textInput`, and `select` theme.json elements — already supported by theme.json parsing and CSS generation, but invisible in the editor — are now surfaced in the Global Styles UI under **Typography → Elements** and **Colors → Elements** as "Citations", "Inputs", and "Selects". Users can set font and text/background color for quote and pullquote citations, text inputs (Search block, comment form fields), and select dropdowns (Archives, Categories) without hand-editing theme.json. To make this possible the shared `ColorPanel` in `@wordpress/block-editor` gained a new `additionalElements` prop so the Global Styles colors screen can inject element rows beyond the built-in Button/Heading/Caption/Link set. No theme.json schema, CSS generation, or PHP behavior changed — this is purely UI exposure of existing element support.
Digest entry: issues/gutenberg/gh-gutenberg-80852.md · Source: WordPress/gutenberg

item.title: #81532: Block editor: add an inserter to the parent selector
item.description:
The block parent selector in the editor toolbar now carries a second button — a plus that inserts a sibling block *after* the currently selected child, without first having to select the parent. Previously the only way to append a sibling from inside a nested block was to know that Enter does it, or to select the parent and hunt for its corner appender or custom toolbar inserter. `BlockParentSelector` now renders the parent button and a standard `Inserter` together inside a `ToolbarGroup`, and Column's default appender was removed as a consequence. This fixes gutenberg#47200 (the long-standing "how do I add another gallery image" complaint) and applies to every block with inner blocks, not just the ones that shipped a bespoke appender.
Digest entry: issues/gutenberg/gh-gutenberg-81532.md · Source: WordPress/gutenberg

item.title: #81631: Env: Fall back to cached docker images when the registry is unreachable
item.description:
wp-env now falls back to locally cached Docker images when the Docker registry cannot be reached during `wp-env start`. The previously unguarded image-pull step no longer aborts startup when the registry is unavailable. This fixes a hard failure that could occur when configuration changes or `--update` is used while the registry is down but cached images already exist.
Digest entry: issues/gutenberg/gh-gutenberg-81631.md · Source: WordPress/gutenberg

item.title: #78909: PHP-Only blocks: forward current post ID to server render
item.description:
PHP-only blocks (server-registered blocks using `supports.autoRegister`, which get an auto-generated `edit` backed by `useServerSideRender`) were previewed in the editor without any post context, so a `render_callback` calling `get_the_ID()` or otherwise relying on the post being edited rendered against the wrong post — or none at all. This change makes the auto-generated `edit` pass the current `postId` block context to the server render request as a `post_id` URL query argument, matching what the older `ServerSideRender` component has always done. It also forces `postId` into the block type's `usesContext` so the value is actually available, regardless of what the PHP registration declared. Editor previews of PHP-only blocks now match front-end output for post-dependent render callbacks.
Digest entry: issues/gutenberg/gh-gutenberg-78909.md · Source: WordPress/gutenberg

item.title: #77750: Block Editor: Fix blockGap fallback handling for nested var() fallback values
item.description:
Layout gap fallback resolution in the block editor no longer splits a processed gap string on whitespace, which produced malformed CSS when `styles.spacing.blockGap` in `theme.json` used nested `var()` fallbacks such as `var(--a, var(--b, 1.2rem))`. Splitting on spaces treated the whitespace *inside* the nested `var()` expression as a row/column separator, so editing row-gap or column-gap on a Columns (flex) or Grid block emitted a gap value with unbalanced parentheses. The flex and grid layout definitions now read the row/column values structurally via `getGapBoxControlValueFromStyle()` and resolve them through `getSpacingPresetCssVar()`. Fixes Gutenberg issue #76896.
Digest entry: issues/gutenberg/gh-gutenberg-77750.md · Source: WordPress/gutenberg

item.title: #67657: Deprecate product brand recount methods
item.description:
Two public methods on `WC_Brands` are now deprecated as of WooCommerce 11.2.0: `recount_after_stock_change()` is superseded by the global `wc_recount_after_stock_change()`, and `recount_all_brands()` by `wc_recount_all_terms()`. Both methods keep their signatures and remain callable, but they now emit a `wc_deprecated_function()` notice and delegate straight to the shared term-recount functions instead of carrying their own `product_brand`-specific implementation. This is the cleanup half of PR #67630, which folded product-brand counting into WooCommerce's shared term recount path and left these two methods with no internal callers. Carries the `developer advisory` label and ships a `minor`/`update` changelog entry.
Digest entry: issues/woocommerce/gh-woocommerce-67657.md · Source: woocommerce/woocommerce

item.title: REST API: Bind finalize sub-size file names to their sideload.
item.description:
The REST attachments controller's `finalize` endpoint previously stored whatever sub-size file names a client sent, without checking that a sideload had actually produced them for that attachment. Because those names are later resolved against the attachment's upload directory and then read or deleted, a finalize request could record — and later cause core to operate on — a file the upload never created. This changeset makes `sideload_item()` record every file name it generates under a new `_wp_sideloaded_file` post meta key, and makes `finalize_item()` accept a name only if a prior sideload recorded it, it is the attachment's own attached file, or it is already present in the attachment's metadata; anything else fails with `rest_invalid_sub_size_file` (HTTP 400) before any metadata is written. Sideloads are also now pinned to the attachment's own uploads subdirectory via an `upload_dir` filter, so generated names live in the directory they are later resolved against, and the `image_size` / `sub_sizes` schemas are tightened considerably.
Digest entry: issues/wp-core/gh-wordpress-develop-3767a6c06a.md · Source: WordPress/wordpress-develop

item.title: WordPress Contributor Toolkit 1.0: A smoother workflow for your first Core contribution
item.description:
WordPress Contributor Toolkit 1.0 is an experimental desktop app that guides first-time contributors through setting up a full `wordpress-develop` environment and completing a Core contribution. It bundles the required Git, Node.js, and npm tooling, so contributors do not need to install Git, Node.js, npm, or Docker. The 1.0 workflow covers linking a Trac ticket, reviewing existing pull requests and patches, applying and testing work, creating a diff or pull request, and updating the site to latest trunk. It is available for Windows, macOS on Apple Silicon, and Linux.
Digest entry: issues/dev-notes/make-core-125508.md · Source: Make WordPress Core

item.title: Accessibility Improvements in WordPress 7.1
item.description:
WordPress 7.1's accessibility work lands 45 fixes and enhancements in core plus 43 in the editor, with three items that carry developer-visible consequences. Core gains a standardized mechanism for accessible tooltips (#51006), already applied to metabox order buttons (#50921) and the login "Remember Me" control (#55343). List tables now treat the post title cell as the row header instead of the selection checkbox (#32892, #65743), and KSES learns to allow invoker command attributes (#64576) and the `autofocus` attribute on `dialog` elements (#65491). The release also ships a documented, known accessibility regression: the media library switches from a "Load more" button to infinite scroll by default, with an opt-out per user and via the existing `media_library_infinite_scrolling` filter. The block editor adds new Tabs (#80163) and Playlist (#80203) blocks and a decorative-image toggle on the Image block (#78064).
Digest entry: issues/dev-notes/make-core-125420.md · Source: Make WordPress Core

item.title: WordPress 7.2 Call for Volunteers
item.description:
The 7.2 release cycle has entered planning, with a proposed final release date of Wednesday, December 9, 2026 and a milestone schedule running from alpha through dry run. The post calls for volunteers to join a smaller, focused Release Squad and to coordinate with Make Team Reps. It matters to teams planning upgrades, testing, and release-related work because it sets the expected 7.2 timeline and contribution path.
Digest entry: issues/dev-notes/make-core-125465.md · Source: Make WordPress Core

item.title: WordPress 7.1 Release Candidate 3
item.description:
The third release candidate for WordPress 7.1 is available for testing and contains more than 90 updates and fixes since the first release candidate, including 37 Editor changes and 57 Core changes. It is the latest pre-release milestone before the scheduled final release on August 19, 2026, and it marks the hard string freeze for the 7.1 release cycle. Developers should evaluate it on non-production sites and report issues to Trac or the Alpha/Beta support forums.
Digest entry: issues/dev-notes/make-core-125449.md · Source: Make WordPress Core

item.title: What’s new in Gutenberg 23.7? (05 August)
item.description:
Gutenberg 23.7 is a consolidation release: most of the cycle went into visual editor fixes rather than new surface area. The Gallery block's dynamic mode — new in 23.6 — gets its ambiguous "Convert to images" toolbar button renamed to "Detach" with an explanatory modal (#80727), and dynamic-mode conversion now collapses into a single undo level (#80665). The experimental Global Styles inheritance UI, which reflects inherited values in block inspector controls, has been moved behind an opt-in toggle on the Gutenberg Experiments screen (#80815). Alongside that: a new `responsiveEditingEnabled` editor setting, `editableRoot` demoted from a public block support to a private block setting, and `Group`/`GroupLabel` subcomponents added across Combobox, Select and SelectControl.
Digest entry: issues/dev-notes/make-core-125396.md · Source: Make WordPress Core

item.title: WordPress 7.0.4 Release
item.description:
This WordPress security release fixes an authenticated Author+ remote code execution vulnerability triggered by a malicious file upload on sites that use Imagick and Ghostscript. The announcement recommends updating immediately because the issue allows remote code execution. The fix is also being backported to the 4.7 branch and the 7.1 RC3 release.
Digest entry: issues/security/wp-news-security-21371.md · Source: WordPress News

item.title: WordPress 7.0.3 release
item.description:
WordPress 7.0.3 is a security-only release fixing 12 separately reported vulnerabilities, headlined by a pre-authentication reflected XSS on the login screen that could be chained to PHP code execution (CVE-2026-64638 / GHSA-52p2-r8wf-jcrf). The rest are lower-privilege issues: four Contributor+ stored XSS vectors (the emoji settings element, the Post Content block, Quick Edit on large-user sites, the Post Date block), an Author+ CSS injection through a bypass of core's safe CSS attribute filter, a multisite privilege escalation letting an ordinary user create a new site where registration is open, and several information-disclosure and validation bypasses — password-protected post comments leaking through the Latest Comments block, post slug enumeration, notes disclosed in comment feeds, an email-confirmation flow bypass, and an SSRF in URL validation that permitted requests to link-local ranges. Because the login-screen bug is reachable without authentication and reportedly has a path to code execution, this is an update-now release rather than a routine minor. Fixes are being backported to every branch still eligible for security fixes (through 4.7), and 7.1 RC2 ships the applicable patches.
Digest entry: issues/security/wp-news-security-21327.md · Source: WordPress News

item.title: 40,000 WordPress Sites affected by Authentication Bypass Vulnerability in User Profile Builder WordPress Plugin

item.title: TrueBooker <= 1.2.3 - Missing Authorization to Unauthenticated Arbitrary Password Reset via 'truebooker_wp_user_id'
item.description:

item.title: TrueBooker <= 1.2.3 - Missing Authorization to Unauthenticated Arbitrary Password Reset via 'tbab-userid'
item.description:
TrueBooker <= 1.2.3 allowed unauthenticated attackers to reset arbitrary user passwords by supplying a `tbab-userid` value without proving ownership of the target account. Version 1.2.4 fixes the improper password reset validation.

item.title: AI Copilot – Content Generator <= 1.5.6 - Unauthenticated Privilege Escalation via Custom Workflow Route
item.description:
The AI Copilot – Content Generator plugin has an authorization bypass that allows unauthenticated visitors to create an administrator account. The issue occurs when a malicious workflow is saved and executed through the plugin's custom workflow route, using a `wp_create_user` action node with `role=administrator`. The plugin's nonce check is not a reliable authorization barrier because the `waic-nonce` value is exposed in public frontend JavaScript as `WAIC_DATA.waicNonce` when the `[aiwu-form]` shortcode or public chatbot is rendered. No patched version is listed, so affected sites should treat this as an active site-takeover risk.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-e28ae1a3-abc6-484c-abc7-1e0b958fa30b.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: WordPress Core <= 7.0.2 - Unauthenticated Reflected Cross-Site Scripting via log Parameter
item.description:
WordPress core's login screen reflects the submitted `log` value (the username field on `wp-login.php`) back into authentication error messages without sufficient escaping, allowing an unauthenticated attacker to inject arbitrary JavaScript that executes in a victim's browser. Because the payload has to arrive with the login POST, exploitation requires tricking a visitor into submitting a crafted request — typically an auto-submitting form on an attacker-controlled page — which is why it scores 6.1 rather than higher. The fix hardens sanitization/escaping of the login error output. Notably, the vulnerable code reaches back to 4.7.0, so patched builds were shipped simultaneously for every branch from 4.7 through 7.0.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-278da117-fe04-45d6-86d4-e71fe6536032.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: WordPress Core <= 7.0.2 - Authenticated (Contributor+) Stored Cross-Site Scripting via Emoji Settings Element
item.description:
WordPress core allowed a stored cross-site scripting payload to be smuggled into post content via the emoji settings element, because submitted post content was not sufficiently restricted. Any authenticated user at Contributor level or above could save a post carrying the payload; the script then executes when someone previews that post. Because Contributors cannot publish, the realistic trigger is an Editor or Administrator previewing a pending submission for review — meaning the script runs in a higher-privileged session. The fix shipped as a coordinated security release across every branch WordPress still backports to, from 4.7 through 7.0.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-5faaf7d1-2012-42d5-affa-a5ff3388d25a.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: WordPress Core <= 7.0.2 - Authenticated (Subscriber+) Missing Authorization to Arbitrary Site Creation on Multisite
item.description:
WordPress multisite honors a network-wide signup policy (the `registration` site option: `none`, `user`, `blog`, or `all`), but the `gimmeanotherblog` signup stage in `wp-signup.php` did not verify that policy before processing the request. On a network configured to allow user registration only (`registration` = `user`), any logged-in user at Subscriber level or above could POST the `gimmeanotherblog` stage and create a new site anyway, bypassing the network admin's intent. The fix adds the missing active-signup check to that code path. Single-site installs are not affected in any way; only multisite networks are.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-80f92f7f-72e7-4d83-9ceb-ed0e11fb8003.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: WordPress Core <= 7.0.2 - Authenticated (Contributor+) Stored Cross-Site Scripting via Quick Edit
item.description:
WordPress core did not sufficiently escape user display names when rendering the Quick Edit (inline edit) UI on admin list tables, allowing a user who controls their own display name — Contributor role and above — to store markup that executes in the browser of any higher-privileged user who opens the affected list screen. Because a display name is persisted on the user record and re-rendered on every load of the screen, this is a stored (persistent) XSS in the wp-admin origin, not a reflected one. Wordfence notes the issue only manifests on sites with a large number of users, so the vulnerable rendering path is the alternate author-field markup core emits once a site crosses its large-user-count threshold rather than the ordinary author `<select>`. The fix is output escaping, shipped as a coordinated security release across every supported branch back to 4.7.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-92babbbf-74bd-474f-9057-c5022a7d64c7.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: WordPress Core <= 7.0.2 - Unauthenticated Sensitive Information Exposure via Comment Feeds
item.description:
WordPress core leaks the contents of internal notes through its public comment feeds. The comment feed output was built without excluding note-type entries, so anything written as an internal note on a post was serialized into the RSS/Atom comment feed alongside ordinary approved comments — readable by anyone, with no authentication and no interaction from a privileged user. The fix, shipped as a coordinated security release across every maintained branch, restricts comment feed output so internal notes are no longer included. Sites that never used internal notes have nothing to disclose, but the vulnerable code path is present in every listed version.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-c3f9898b-0aa0-4dd1-9298-96c853dbef5c.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: WordPress Core <= 7.0.2 - Authenticated (Author+) CSS Injection
item.description:
WordPress core does not sufficiently sanitize user-supplied CSS in post content, allowing an authenticated user with Author-level capabilities or above to inject arbitrary CSS that is then rendered to other visitors on the front end. Because the injected rules are served as part of the post output, an attacker can restyle or visually rewrite pages for readers — overlaying, hiding, or replacing content that the author would not otherwise be permitted to control. The fix tightens sanitization of user-supplied CSS and has been backported across every supported (and long-tail) branch from the 4.7 line forward. This is a privilege-boundary issue, not a remote/unauthenticated one: it matters on any site where Author is not a fully trusted role.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-c83a2c4d-a264-49ec-85f1-e3f48715d725.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: WordPress Core <= 7.0.2 - Authenticated (Subscriber+) Email Change Confirmation Bypass
item.description:
WordPress core validated a changed email address inconsistently on user-profile updates, so an authenticated user at Subscriber level or above could set a new address on their own account without completing the ownership-confirmation step core normally requires. Instead of parking the address in a pending state and waiting for the confirmation link to be followed, the affected path wrote the new address to the account directly. The fix makes validation of the submitted email consistent across the profile-update paths, so the confirmation handshake is enforced. It is a self-service bypass — the attacker changes their own account's email, not another user's — which is why it lands at CVSS 4.3 rather than in account-takeover territory.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-cac1c1fa-7d6c-43c3-885e-9be320cb8f83.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: WordPress Core <= 7.0.2 - Unauthenticated Blind Server-Side Request Forgery
item.description:
Wordfence disclosed an unauthenticated blind SSRF in WordPress core affecting every release from 4.7.0 through 7.0.2. Core's outbound-request validation does not block all reserved and internal IP address ranges, so an unauthenticated attacker can induce the site to issue HTTP requests to attacker-chosen destinations — including hosts on the server's own private network — with the request originating from the web application rather than the attacker. The vulnerability is *blind*: the response body is not returned to the attacker, so the practical impact is enumeration of internal hosts, port/service discovery, and one-way interaction with internal endpoints that would otherwise be unreachable from the internet. Core shipped fixes across 24 maintenance branches (4.7.34 through 7.0.3).
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-cddbb0f8-fc73-46d7-80af-edb69227084f.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: Formidable Digital Signatures <= 3.0.6 - Unauthenticated Arbitrary File Deletion via Signature Field
item.description:
Formidable Digital Signatures <= 3.0.6 has an unauthenticated arbitrary file deletion vulnerability in the plugin's `delete_file` function. Insufficient file path validation allows an attacker to delete files on the server by sending a crafted filename in `item_meta[field_id][content]` together with the `delete_saved_image` flag during a normal entry-creation POST on a form that accepts anonymous submissions. The issue is fixed in version 3.1. Sites using the plugin should upgrade immediately.

item.title: WordPress Core <= 7.0.3 - Authenticated (Author+) Remote Code Execution via Malicious File Upload
item.description:
WordPress core's Imagick image editor accepted uploaded files whose real content did not match their WordPress-approved extension. `WP_Image_Editor_Imagick::load()` handed the file (or stream) to Imagick without sufficient validation, so ImageMagick could identify it as a PostScript-family or compressed delegate format from magic bytes, an embedded format specifier, or decompressed content — and dispatch it to an external delegate such as Ghostscript. Because this happens automatically during attachment metadata generation, any user with `upload_files` (Author and above) could upload a crafted "image" and reach remote code execution on sites running the Imagick editor with Ghostscript available. The patched releases tighten validation in that load path so the format Imagick acts on is constrained rather than inferred from attacker-controlled content.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-3f6b435b-d8b4-434b-8cac-cc3adbc437eb.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: Wishlist Member X <= 3.34.1 - Unauthenticated Account Takeover via 'mergewith' Parameter
item.description:
Wishlist Member versions up to 3.34.1 allow an unauthenticated attacker to take over an existing WordPress account by passing an arbitrary user ID in the `mergewith` POST parameter during registration. The plugin's `wpm_register()` function checks the registration cookie only against the `reg` GET parameter and does not verify that `mergewith` points to a temporary or incomplete registrant tied to the current registration transaction. The attacker-controlled value is then used to update the target user's username, password, email, first name, and last name, while WordPress password and email change notifications are suppressed. If the supplied `wpm_id` does not match a membership level, the update payload omits the role key, so `wp_update_user()` preserves the target's existing role, including administrator.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-84afe5a7-1bf4-4b83-bf77-efbb003a30cd.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: RapiSafe <= 1.0.4 - Unauthenticated Arbitrary File Deletion via 'rsmfcf7_session' and 'file_name' Parameters
item.description:
RapiSafe's upload-removal AJAX handler allows unauthenticated attackers to delete arbitrary server files because it trusts client-supplied session and file-name values without adequate path validation. The handler's nonce is exposed in public JavaScript, so an attacker can obtain it from any Contact Form 7 page that renders a RapiSafe upload field. No patch is available, so the practical response is to remove or disable the plugin.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-49f67bbb-cbd0-40ae-ae00-9cb72b041e22.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: 6Storage Rentals <= 2.27.0 - Unauthenticated Account Takeover via 'email' Parameter
item.description:
The 6Storage Rentals plugin exposes an unauthenticated account takeover flaw in the `six_storage_create_wp_user()` AJAX handler. The handler is reachable without authentication and can establish a session for any WordPress user whose email address is supplied. This allows an attacker to log in as an existing account, including an administrator, without credentials.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-94e987be-bdfc-4691-b250-2b7d7249df0a.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: User Session Synchronizer <= 1.4.0 - Unauthenticated Authentication Bypass to Account Takeover via 'ussync-key', 'ussync-token', and 'ussync-ref' Parameters
item.description:
User Session Synchronizer's session synchronization handler can be abused by an unauthenticated attacker to impersonate any user, including administrators. The handler trusts attacker-controlled `ussync-key`, `ussync-token`, and `ussync-ref` request parameters without nonce, capability, or shared-secret validation. When an unregistered `ussync-key` is supplied, fallback behavior makes the encryption key and referer check predictable, allowing a crafted `ussync-ref` value to trigger `wp_set_auth_cookie()` for a matched user. No patch is reported, so affected installations should be treated as potentially compromised.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-cbc32e6d-47c5-4050-ba77-5a54203fe56a.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: User Profile Builder <= 3.16.4 - Unauthenticated Authentication Bypass via Type Confusion to Administrator Account Takeover via 'username' Parameter
item.description:
User Profile Builder's registration flow calls `absint()` on the return value of `wp_insert_user()` *before* testing it with `is_wp_error()`. When core rejects a registration — specifically for a username of 61–70 characters — it returns a `WP_Error` object, but `absint()` has already coerced that object to the integer `1`, so the `is_wp_error()` guard never fires and execution continues as if user ID 1 had just been created. The plugin then issues its transient-backed autologin nonce bound to user ID 1, letting an unauthenticated visitor log in as the site's administrator. Fixed in 3.16.5; anything up to and including 3.16.4 is exploitable with a single crafted registration submission and no authentication.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-9f606fba-f779-42ea-a160-6c3b20dc5e79.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: TrueBooker <= 1.2.6 - Unauthenticated Account Takeover via Insecure Direct Object Reference in 'truebooker_wp_user_id' Parameter
item.description:
TrueBooker's `add_front_user_update()` AJAX handler is exposed to unauthenticated requests and trusts a caller-supplied `truebooker_wp_user_id` parameter, passing it straight to `wp_update_user()` with no authentication or ownership check. Any anonymous visitor can therefore rewrite the email address on any account on the site, including an administrator's. Once the email is changed, the attacker triggers WordPress's own lost-password flow and receives the reset link at their own inbox, completing a full administrator takeover. Fixed in 1.2.7; everything up to and including 1.2.6 is exploitable.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-f0d3f7cb-4974-4b0f-9658-1895e5966276.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: Link Library <= 7.9.4 - Unauthenticated Arbitrary File Deletion via link_url Parameter
item.description:
Link Library's link-deletion routine accepted an unvalidated file path from the `link_url` parameter, allowing unauthenticated arbitrary file deletion when the optional local-file deletion setting was enabled and an administrator permanently deleted a submitted link. The vulnerability can lead to remote code execution if a critical file such as `wp-config.php` is deleted. The patched release corrects the path validation in the deletion flow.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-41327dfa-db64-476a-a263-7bd4f69fb857.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: Solace Extra <= 1.6.0 - Missing Authorization to Unauthenticated Site Content Deletion and Unauthorized Demo Import via action-import-zip AJAX Action
item.description:
Solace Extra has a missing capability check on the `import_zip()` AJAX handler, allowing low-privilege users to delete site content and trigger demo imports. The handler is registered for both authenticated and unauthenticated AJAX requests and relies only on an `ajax-nonce` nonce that is exposed on admin pages. This can wipe navigation menus, sidebar widgets, theme mods, and Elementor templates. The patched release addresses the missing authorization.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-4e427c4e-3e27-49e3-ba64-6241b430d5d8.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: Pods <= 3.3.9 - Unauthenticated Privilege Escalation via Authorization Bypass to Admin Methods via 'pods_admin' AJAX Router
item.description:
The Pods plugin had an unauthenticated privilege escalation vulnerability in its `pods_admin` AJAX router. Access checks were funneled through `pods_error()`, which under the JSON meta-box-loader compatibility path only wrote failures to the PHP error log and returned `false` instead of terminating the request. As a result, the method allowlist, nonce verification, login enforcement, and capability gate did not block requests, allowing an unauthenticated attacker to reach admin methods, escalate to Administrator, or overwrite any user's password. The fix restores request termination when authorization checks fail.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-3628032a-3121-45a7-8a78-cfcd8ba6af2f.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: Frontend Admin by DynamiApps <= 3.29.9 - Unauthenticated Privilege Escalation via 'item_id' Parameter
item.description:
The plugin's user-update AJAX flow could be abused to bypass a capability check and take over the default administrator account. The bypass occurred when a non-numeric `item_id` value caused the `edit_user` check to be skipped, allowing a signed ACF objects payload to be processed with a user ID that WordPress coerced to `1`. The fix closes the authorization gap in the user update path.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-01404fad-7b5a-485a-b557-c608fe25e6c9.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: ProSolution WP Client <= 2.0.8 - Unauthenticated Arbitrary File Deletion via 'newfilename' and 'filename' Parameters
item.description:
ProSolution WP Client is vulnerable to unauthenticated arbitrary file deletion caused by insufficient path validation in `proSol_fileDeleteProcess`. An attacker can first call `proSol_fileUploadModalProcess` to poison their session with a path-traversal key, then call `proSol_fileDeleteProcess` using that key as the `filename` parameter. Both steps require only the publicly exposed frontend nonce. Deleting files such as `wp-config.php` can lead to remote code execution.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-4e9698f0-b228-4f4e-838b-c0c0a193d675.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: ProSolution WP Client <= 2.0.10 - Unauthenticated Arbitrary File Upload via Content-Disposition Header Filename Override
item.description:
The ProSolution WP Client plugin has an unauthenticated arbitrary file upload vulnerability in `proSol_handleFileUpload` that can lead to remote code execution. The handler trusts an attacker-controlled `Content-Disposition` header filename, which overrides the allow-listed multipart filename before the file is saved, and a post-save extension check does not delete the already-written file. The nonce required to reach the upload handler is publicly exposed via `wp_localize_script` on front-end pages rendering the job portal shortcode, allowing unauthenticated visitors to bypass that gating check. Sites should update to the patched release immediately.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-3c4a7aef-09ec-4d17-87d6-f507d64e0afa.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: #81787: Command Palette: Allow commands to override the category icon
item.description:
The Command Palette's per-category icon is now a fallback rather than an override. Since #75669 added command categories, every command in the `view` category was force-rendered with the `arrowRight` icon, silently discarding any `icon` the command itself registered. `CommandItem` now resolves `command.icon ?? CATEGORY_FALLBACK_ICONS[ category ]`, so a command that supplies its own icon wins and only iconless commands fall back to the category default. Core's `view` commands were audited alongside the change: the icons that were being registered but never rendered are deleted from source, leaving only "View site" and "Preview in a new tab" overriding the arrow with `external`.
Digest entry: issues/gutenberg/gh-gutenberg-81787.md · Source: WordPress/gutenberg

item.title: #81729: Dashboard: add a Site Health detail page as the dashboard's second route
item.description:
Adds `routes/site-health`, the second route in Gutenberg's experimental Dashboard app, giving the site-health widget an in-app destination instead of only linking out to the classic Site Health screen. The page fetches the six async health tests core exposes over the REST namespace `wp-site-health/v1` and renders them in a DataViews table with sortable/filterable Status and Category badge columns and a per-check description. A new `Details` action in `widgets/site-health/widget.json` points at `admin.php?page=dashboard-wp-admin&p=/site-health` — still a plain anchor, so following it is a full page load until the router-link upgrade lands (#81725). The widget's own fetch list also picks up the previously missing `page-cache` test, and the dashboard route swaps its `Page` `title` prop for a `Breadcrumbs` element.
Digest entry: issues/gutenberg/gh-gutenberg-81729.md · Source: WordPress/gutenberg

item.title: #81738: Dashboard Widgets: resolve widget types without a metadata module
item.description:
`useWidgetTypes()` in `@wordpress/widget-primitives` previously dropped any widget-module record whose `widget_module` was `null`, which forced every bundled Dashboard widget to ship a `widget.ts` stub that exported nothing but its own name. The hook now resolves such a record from its own REST fields — `title`, `description`, `icon`, `actions`, `presentation`, `category`, `help`, `keywords` — as long as the record carries a `render_module`, so a widget can be declared entirely by its `widget.json` manifest. Six bundled widgets (`site-preview`, `welcome`, `news`, `quick-draft`, `hello-dolly`, `site-health`) lose their `widget.ts` as a result. The change also introduces a `DEFAULT_API_VERSION = 1` fallback that applies on both resolution paths, closing a hole where a module omitting `apiVersion` produced an `undefined` masked by the `as WidgetType` cast.

item.title: #81408: RTC: Add fallback identities when user profiles are unavailable
item.description:
Gutenberg's real-time collaboration awareness layer previously assumed `resolveSelect( coreStore ).getCurrentUser()` would always resolve — on sites that remove the `/wp/v2/users` REST routes the request fails, `collaboratorInfo` is never published to the Yjs awareness state, and presence consumers end up reading properties off a missing object. This PR makes `BaseAwarenessState.setCurrentCollaboratorInfo()` tolerate a failed or unusable user response and publish a complete session-scoped fallback identity instead: name `Anonymous User`, `id: null`, slug `anonymous-<clientId>`, and no `avatar_urls` so the existing avatar component renders "AU" initials. Session-specific behavior (cursor color, block highlighting, avatar grouping, notification IDs) keys off the Yjs awareness `clientID` when no WordPress user ID exists. It also adds a runtime type guard, `isCollaboratorInfo()`, so malformed peer-supplied awareness data is excluded from presence and debug output rather than trusted because TypeScript says so.

item.title: #81769: Fields: Export the package stylesheet
item.description:
Adds `./build-style/*` to the `exports` map in `packages/fields/package.json`, so the `@wordpress/fields` stylesheet can be imported as `@wordpress/fields/build-style/style.css`. Previously, that package path was blocked by the exports allowlist, causing bundled fields such as `MediaEdit` to render unstyled without a build error. The PR also adds a README Setup section explaining how to load the required CSS inside and outside WordPress.

item.title: #81358: UI: Add Spinner component
item.description:
A `Spinner` component has been added to `@wordpress/ui`, ported from `@wordpress/components`. It renders the same SVG track-plus-arc structure and 1.4s linear spin, but is styled with WPDS custom properties inside the wp-ui `@layer` cascade and drops the legacy component's hardcoded `margin: 5px 11px 0` and explicit `width`/`height` SVG attributes. The `@wordpress/components` Spinner is now flagged `not-recommended` in Storybook (a formal `@deprecated` pass is planned separately), and the `@wordpress/eslint-plugin` `use-recommended-components` rule now allows `Spinner` from `@wordpress/ui`. The port is a prerequisite for moving validated form controls off private `@wordpress/components` APIs.

item.title: #81653: Site Editor: Use inverted ThemeProvider seed for portaled UI
item.description:
The Site Editor now wraps its layout in an outer root `ThemeProvider` that seeds the admin color scheme's `primary` color and a white content background, while the existing `ThemeProvider` remains nested for the editor chrome. This fixes portaled popovers and modals that render outside the original `ThemeProvider` wrapper and therefore missed the chosen admin scheme's accent colors. It backports the inverted `ThemeProvider` seed pattern from #81296 to trunk. The change is a broad stopgap until portaled components are fully theme-ready.

item.title: #81785: Modal: Stop Escape key propagation on dismiss
item.description:
The `Modal` component in `@wordpress/components` now stops Escape key propagation when it handles the key to dismiss itself. This prevents a single Escape press from also closing an underlying overlay when a modal is opened without closing its originating overlay. The fix also avoids removing the element that the modal should restore focus to. It is a targeted keyboard-behavior bug fix for stacked overlay UIs.

item.title: #81160: Global styles: Register <label> as element
item.description:
This registers `label` as a global-styles element, so `theme.json` can now carry a `styles.elements.label` block that applies to every `<label>` tag on the front end and in the editor — not just labels rendered by core blocks. It continues the recent form-element work in global styles (which already covers `textInput` and `select`), letting a theme style form labels consistently regardless of which blocks or third-party plugins emit the form. To keep the new element styles from being outranked by block defaults, the PR also rewrites the label CSS in Categories, Comments, Post Comments Form, Form Input, and Search to use `:where()` so those defaults sit at zero specificity.

item.title: #80399: UI: Derive Base UI direction from WordPress i18n
item.description:
Direction-sensitive components in the `@wordpress/ui` package now read WordPress's text direction automatically instead of inheriting Base UI's hard-coded LTR default. Base UI seeds its internal direction context to `ltr`, so `Autocomplete`, `Combobox`, `Popover`, `Select`, `Tabs`, and `Tooltip` behaved as LTR in RTL locales — wrong arrow-key order in horizontal `Tabs`, wrong positioning/flip logic for anchored content. A new private `DirectionProvider` util reads `isRTL()` from `@wordpress/i18n` and is wrapped around the six `Root` components whose Base UI internals consume direction, so consumers no longer need to mount and forward a second public direction provider of their own.

item.title: #81373: Global Styles: filter and indicate blocks that have custom styles
item.description:
The Site Editor's **Styles → Blocks** list now marks every block the user has customized with a small dot, and adds a funnel menu beside the search field to narrow the list to just those blocks. Previously the screen rendered every registered block with nothing distinguishing customized ones, so auditing your own global-styles changes meant drilling into blocks one at a time. A block counts as customized when the *user* layer of the global styles config has a real value under either `styles.blocks[ blockName ]` or `settings.blocks[ blockName ]` — so a block-specific color palette marks a block just as a text color does. The dot is paired with a `VisuallyHidden` "Has custom styles" label, which changes the accessible name of those rows.

item.title: #81476: Enable axial gap for Group and restrict to flex and grid layouts.
item.description:
The Group block can now take separate row and column values for `blockGap`, but the split (axial) control is only rendered when the block instance resolves to a `flex` or `grid` layout — flow and constrained Groups keep the single input, since those layouts only ever set `margin-block-start` on children. A new helper, `isAxialBlockGapAllowed()`, makes that decision, and the shared global-styles `DimensionsPanel` gained an `allowAxialBlockGap` prop (defaulting to `true`, so Global Styles keeps axial controls for the Group block regardless of variation). The PR also corrects two server-side bugs: `WP_Theme_JSON` previously dropped an axial `blockGap` entirely unless *both* `top` and `left` were set, and flow/constrained layouts were writing the full `"<row> <column>"` shorthand into `margin-block-start`. Responsive grid column math now reads the horizontal (`left`) value instead of the concatenated shorthand.

item.title: #80417: Components: Align legacy form control focus rings with WPDS
item.description:
The shared focus treatment for legacy `InputBase`-derived form controls (`InputControl`, `SelectControl`, `CustomSelectControl` and everything built on them) moves from an Emotion-generated border + box-shadow combination to the WPDS outset focus ring, so `@wordpress/components` controls visually match their `@wordpress/ui` replacements ahead of consumer migration. The old style — a darkened 1px border plus a 0.5px box-shadow to fake a 1.5px stroke, with a transparent `outline` as a Windows High Contrast Mode fallback — is replaced by a single `outset-ring__focus()` mixin call in package Sass that uses the `--wpds-border-width-focus` and `--wpds-color-stroke-focus` tokens. Because the new ring paints outside the control, DataViews' filter operator `SelectControl` had to stop clipping it: `overflow: hidden` becomes `min-width: 0`. Validated (invalid-state) controls also switch the custom property they override to recolor the focus ring, from `--wp-components-color-accent` to `--focus-color`.

item.title: #81697: Add `__unstable_wp_sync_storage` filter for pluggable storage backends
item.description:
Adds the `__unstable_wp_sync_storage` filter to Gutenberg's experimental real-time collaboration code, letting plugins replace the default `WP_Sync_Post_Meta_Storage` implementation with a custom `WP_Sync_Storage` backend. The default behavior remains post-meta storage, but the filter gives an integration point for plugins that want to avoid the cache invalidation associated with storing sync data in post meta. The filter is explicitly unstable because the collaboration sync interface is still experimental and may change.

item.title: 600,000 WordPress Sites Affected by Arbitrary File Upload Vulnerability in Forminator Forms WordPress Plugin
item.description:
Forminator Forms fixed a critical unauthenticated arbitrary file upload vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-15748, that allowed attackers to upload arbitrary files, including executable PHP files, to a vulnerable site. The flaw could lead to remote code execution and full site compromise. It was exploitable only when a Forminator form contained both a File Upload field and a Select field. The patched release is 1.56.2.

item.title: Contact Form, Survey, Quiz & Popup Form Builder – ARForms <= 1.8.5 - Unauthenticated PHP Object Injection
item.description:
ARForms fixed an unauthenticated PHP object injection vulnerability caused by deserializing untrusted data from form submissions. The flaw allowed an attacker to submit crafted serialized object data, but exploitation requires a POP chain from another installed plugin or theme. The patched release addresses the unsafe deserialization path. Sites using the affected plugin should update promptly.

item.title: Forminator Forms <= 1.56.1 - Unauthenticated Arbitrary File Upload via Forged Upload Field Configuration
item.description:
Forminator Forms versions up to 1.56.1 allowed unauthenticated arbitrary file upload through the `handle_file_upload` function. The plugin's dangerous-extension blocklist used exact-key matching that could be bypassed with pipe-alternative MIME type keys, and a public submission handler accepted attacker-controlled upload field configuration from a forged Select field value. This could let an attacker upload files that may be executable and achieve remote code execution. The issue is fixed in 1.56.2.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-263ac05d-f1ca-46e3-a43e-3b45eb8066d4.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: TrueBooker <= 1.2.6 - Unauthenticated Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key to Account Takeover to 'truebooker_wp_user_id' Parameter
item.description:
TrueBooker – Appointment Booking and Scheduler System exposes an `admin_user_create_cus` AJAX action that performs no authentication, capability, or nonce check before handing the request-supplied `truebooker_wp_user_id` value to `wp_update_user()`. Because the target user ID is entirely attacker-controlled, an unauthenticated request can rewrite the email address on any account on the site — administrators included. Once the email is changed, the attacker triggers WordPress's stock lost-password flow, receives the reset link at their own address, and takes over the account outright. Fixed in 1.2.6's successor, 1.2.7; anything at or below 1.2.6 is exploitable with a single unauthenticated POST.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-73251a74-5be3-446b-8e0a-ff2d1484c467.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence
